images.title: Up and down to 7
images.purpose: Show that adding 1 up to 7 and back down to 1 gives 7 × 7 = 49.
images.composition: One row of 13 bars on a common baseline, centred, with the result line below.
images.exact_structure: 13 vertical bars of equal width and equal gaps on one baseline, with heights 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1 units, each unit exactly the same height. The 12 bars other than the middle one are teal #0072B2; the tallest middle bar is amber #E69F00. Two labels only. Exactly 13 bars.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
bars whose heights do not rise by one unit, or a peak that is not 7 units
images.takeaway: Going up to 7 and back down adds up to 7 × 7 = 49.
images.description: Thirteen bars rising 1 to 7 and falling back to 1, the tallest in amber, with 7 × 7 = 49 below.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the peak and say which number the whole sum is multiplied.

image_decisions.why: An up-and-down staircase makes the n × n rule visible at a glance.
